title: incident signal federation and failure taxonomy workbench
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a reusable workbench that federates incident signals (traces, metrics, logs) into a canonical failure taxonomy for the inference stack. Goal: enable day-0 dashboards and drilldowns that accurately attribute user-visible errors and latency to: network timeouts, overload/backpressure, model errors (OOM, rejection, bad logits), HTTP/gRPC status codes, and internal runtime exits. The workbench should provide: 1) a tracehook enrichment spec and SDK snippets for services to attach model/session metadata and KV-cache hints; 2) a metrics/log ingestion pipeline transformation that maps provider codes (e.g., gRPC code, model-exit-code) to our canonical failure classes; 3) Grafana/Looker dashboards and a lightweight exploratory UI for oncall to pivot by failure class, model version, route, and hardware pool. This ticket covers design, prototyping, instrumentation changes, and first-pass dashboards for critical routes (generate/chat/embed).

decisions: Adopt a three-layer failure taxonomy: transport (HTTP/gRPC codes, network timeouts), runtime (overload, queueing/backpressure, OOM), model (model rejections, incorrect outputs, tokenization errors).
Map provider-specific codes to canonical classes via a normalization table maintained in the ingestion pipeline. Runtime teams will supply mappings as PRs to a central repo.
Tracehook spec will be minimal and backward-compatible: new attributes are optional strings/booleans; SDK will include helpers to set them where available.
Dashboards will default to 'failure-class first' view to help oncall narrow scope quickly; a secondary view will be 'route/model first' for product owners.
